source_clauses.verbatim: It should have three legs that fold in close to the body, so the whole thing becomes narrow and compact when I put it away.
Everything should stay attached while it is folded.
I do not want to take anything off to fold it, or loose pieces to look after.
When I want to use it, I should be able to open it by hand, following a sequence that makes sense as I go.
The three legs should end up spread apart in different directions so they give the stand a usable footprint on the desk.
Nothing should come apart or fall off while I am opening it, and I should not need tools, a motor, or any other equipment to do it.
Once it is open, it needs to stay open on its own.
I should not have to hold the legs while I use it, and they should not be able to fold back, twist aside, or come off.
Nothing should turn on its own, shift out of place, or move in some other direction I was not expecting.
Before it can be folded again I want to have to do something deliberate, so it does not collapse just because I knocked it.
After that deliberate release, it should fold back down to the same compact shape it started in.
The opening and folding sequence should be repeatable, with all normal parts remaining attached and without anything needing to be removed and put back on.
It is meant to hold a small object on my desk while I am working.
It should also be something that can genuinely be built as a product and put together in a sensible order, and stay together through normal opening and folding.

scenarios.name: Folding for storage
scenarios.system_boundary: Inside: the folding stand with its legs and body. Outside: the user's hands and the desk surface on which the stand may be placed or rested.

scenarios.name: Opening for use
scenarios.system_boundary: Inside: the folding stand with its legs and body. Outside: the user's hands and the desk surface on which the stand will be placed.

scenarios.name: Holding an object while working
scenarios.system_boundary: Inside: the folding stand. Outside: the desk surface (supporting the stand) and the small object placed on the stand.
scenarios.environment: on a desk while user works

scenarios.name: Assembly as a product
scenarios.system_boundary: Inside: the product to be assembled (the stand). Outside: the assembly personnel, tools/fixtures, and the factory or assembly environment.

must_reach: the stand to open and fold it

Not specified; only that it must be built in a sensible order

ambiguities.statement: What constitutes a 'small object' in terms of size and weight?
ambiguities.resolvable_when: when the product's intended use is clarified by stakeholders

ambiguities.statement: What does 'sequence that makes sense' mean? Is there a required order or is any intuitive order acceptable?
ambiguities.resolvable_when: upon user testing or specific design guidance

ambiguities.statement: The phrase 'do something deliberate' to release the folded state could be interpreted as requiring a separate lock or latch, but the exact action is not specified.
ambiguities.resolvable_when: when the design concept is chosen and tested

assumptions.statement: The desk surface is stable and provides a firm support for the stand.
assumptions.why: To allow the stand to remain open and stable while holding an object.
assumptions.would_be_invalidated_by: If the desk surface is uneven or unstable, the stand might not stay open as required.

assumptions.statement: The user has sufficient manual dexterity to operate the folding mechanism by hand.
assumptions.why: The request requires opening and folding by hand without tools.
assumptions.would_be_invalidated_by: If the mechanism requires strength or dexterity beyond typical human capability.

assumptions.statement: The 'sequence that makes sense' can be designed to be intuitive and repeatable.
assumptions.why: The request demands a sequence that makes sense and is repeatable.
assumptions.would_be_invalidated_by: If the mechanism cannot be made intuitive or if it requires excessive force or complex steps.
